translations.literal: It is called "The Seal of Commissioned Orders," bluish jade, square, three cun seven fen on a side, one cun eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The "Seal of Commissioned Orders" is of bluish jade, three cun seven fen square and one cun eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 交龍紐，高二寸五分。

translations.literal: Intertwined-dragon knob, two cun five fen high.
translations.idiomatic: Its knob is intertwined dragons two cun five fen high.

sentences.zh: 曰「廣運之寶」，金，方二寸四分，厚八分。

translations.literal: It is called "The Seal of Vast Fortune," gold, square, two cun four fen on a side, eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The "Seal of Vast Fortune" is of gold, two cun four fen square and eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 交龍紐，高一寸五分。

translations.literal: Intertwined-dragon knob, one cun five fen high.
translations.idiomatic: Its knob is intertwined dragons one cun five fen high.

sentences.zh: 高宗御制國朝傳寶記曰：「國朝受天命，采古制為璽。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor's imperial composition "Record of the Dynastic Transmission Seals" says: "Our dynasty received Heaven's mandate and, following ancient models, fashioned seals.
translations.idiomatic: In his imperial composition "Record of the Dynastic Transmission Seals," the Qianlong Emperor wrote: "Our dynasty received Heaven's mandate and fashioned seals according to ancient models.

sentences.zh: 掌以宮殿監正，襲以重盝，承以魨幾，設交泰殿中，以次左右列，當用則內閣請而用之。

translations.literal: They are kept by the director of the Palace Directorate, passed down in layered cases, placed on cushion stands, set in the Hall of Union and Peace, arrayed left and right in order; when needed, the Grand Secretariat requests them for use.
translations.idiomatic: They are kept by the director of the Palace Directorate, stored in layered cases on cushion stands in the Hall of Union and Peace, arranged in order to left and right; when a seal is required, the Grand Secretariat requests it.

sentences.zh: 其質有玉、有金、有栴檀木。

translations.literal: Their materials include jade, gold, and sandalwood.
translations.idiomatic: They are made of jade, gold, or sandalwood.

sentences.zh: 玉之品有白、有青、有碧。

translations.literal: The kinds of jade include white, bluish, and green.
translations.idiomatic: The jades vary in color: white, bluish, and green.

sentences.zh: 紐有交龍、有盤龍、有蹲龍。

translations.literal: The knobs include intertwined dragons, coiled dragons, and crouching dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The knobs may be intertwined dragons, coiled dragons, or crouching dragons.

sentences.zh: 其文自太宗文皇帝以前，專用國書，既乃兼用古篆。

translations.literal: Their inscriptions before Emperor Taizong the Literary Emperor used only the national script; thereafter both that and ancient seal script were used.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Literary Emperor Taizong, only the Manchu script was used on them; afterward ancient seal script was added as well.

sentences.zh: 其大小自方六寸至二寸一分不一。

translations.literal: Their sizes vary from six cun square down to two cun one fen square.
translations.idiomatic: Their dimensions range from six cun square down to as small as two cun one fen square.

sentences.zh: 嘗考大清會典，載御寶二十有九，今交泰殿所貯三十有九。

translations.literal: I once examined the Collected Statutes of the Great Qing, which record twenty-nine imperial seals; now those stored in the Hall of Union and Peace number thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Statutes of the Great Qing list twenty-nine imperial seals, yet thirty-nine are now kept in the Hall of Union and Peace.

sentences.zh: 會典又云：『宮內收貯者六，內庫收貯者二十有三。』

translations.literal: The Statutes also say: "Six are kept within the palace, and twenty-three are kept in the inner storehouse."
translations.idiomatic: The Statutes further state that six were kept within the palace and twenty-three in the inner storehouse.

sentences.zh: 今則皆貯交泰殿，數與地皆失實。

translations.literal: Now all are stored in the Hall of Union and Peace; both the count and the locations are inaccurate.
translations.idiomatic: Today all are kept in the Hall of Union and Peace, so both the numbers and the storage locations given in the record are wrong.

sentences.zh: 至謂『皇帝奉天之寶』即傳國璽，兩郊大祀及聖節宮中告天青詞用之，此語尤誕謬。

translations.literal: As for saying that the "Emperor's Seal of Obeying Heaven" is the seal of dynastic transmission, used for suburban sacrifices at both altars and for blue prayers announcing Heaven in the palace on imperial birthdays—this statement is especially absurd.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that the "Emperor's Seal of Obeying Heaven" is the dynastic transmission seal, used at the great suburban sacrifices and for blue prayer texts to Heaven in the palace on imperial birthdays, is especially absurd.

sentences.zh: 大祀遵古禮，用祝版署名而不用寶。

translations.literal: Great sacrifices follow ancient rites and use prayer boards signed by name, not seals.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices follow ancient ritual and use signed prayer boards, not seals.

sentences.zh: 聖節宮中未嘗有告天事，或道籙祝釐，時一行之，亦不過偶存其教耳，未嘗命文人為青詞，亦未嘗用寶。

translations.literal: In the palace on imperial birthdays there has never been an announcement to Heaven; occasionally Daoist registers and prayers for blessing are performed, but that is only to preserve the teaching in passing—literati have never been ordered to compose blue prayers, nor have seals ever been used.
translations.idiomatic: The palace has never conducted announcements to Heaven on imperial birthdays; Daoist liturgies are performed only occasionally, as a vestige of the faith, and scholars have never been commissioned to write blue prayer texts, nor have seals been used for such purposes.

sentences.zh: 且此璽孰非世之傳守，而專以一寶為傳國璽，亦不經。

translations.literal: Moreover, which of these seals is not handed down and guarded through the ages? To single out one seal alone as the seal of dynastic transmission is also unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, every one of these seals is handed down through the generations; to designate a single seal alone as the dynastic transmission seal makes no sense.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣修會典諸臣無宿學卓識，復未嘗請旨取裁，僅沿明時內監所書冊檔，承譌襲謬，遂至於此。

translations.literal: This is because the officials who compiled the Statutes lacked deep learning and outstanding insight, and never sought imperial guidance; they merely followed the ledgers written by Ming eunuchs, perpetuating errors until matters reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: This happened because the compilers of the Statutes lacked deep scholarship and sound judgment and never sought the throne's ruling; they simply followed Ming eunuch ledgers, perpetuating errors until the record became what it is.

sentences.zh: 甚矣紀載之難也。

translations.literal: How difficult it is to record things accurately!
translations.idiomatic: How difficult accurate historical recording truly is!

sentences.zh: 且會典所不載者，復有『受命於天既壽永昌』一璽，不知何時附藏殿內，反置之正中。

translations.literal: Moreover, among items not recorded in the Statutes there is also a seal inscribed "Having Received the Mandate from Heaven, Long Life and Eternal Prosperity," which was placed in the hall at some unknown time and set in the very center.
translations.idiomatic: The Statutes also fail to mention a seal inscribed "Having Received the Mandate from Heaven, Long Life and Eternal Prosperity," which was placed in the hall at some unknown date and set in the central position.

sentences.zh: 按其詞雖類古所傳秦璽，而篆文拙俗，非李斯蟲鳥之舊明甚。

translations.literal: Judging by its text, though it resembles the Qin seal handed down in antiquity, the seal script is crude and vulgar; it is clearly not in the old style of Li Si's insect-and-bird script.
translations.idiomatic: Its inscription resembles the Qin seal of legend, but the seal script is crude and vulgar and clearly not the insect-and-bird script of Li Si's day.

sentences.zh: 獨玉質瑩潔如截肪，方得黍尺四寸四分，厚得方之三。

translations.literal: Only the jade is lustrous and pure as sliced fat; its face measures four cun four fen on the millet-foot ruler, and its thickness is one-third of the face.
translations.idiomatic: Only the jade itself is lustrous and pure as sliced fat; the face measures four cun four fen on the standard foot, and the thickness is one-third of the width.

sentences.zh: 以為良玉不易得則信矣，若論寶，無論非秦璽，即真秦璽，亦何足貴！

translations.literal: It is true that fine jade is hard to obtain; but as for being a treasure—whether it is not the Qin seal or even if it were the genuine Qin seal, what is there to prize in it!
translations.idiomatic: Fine jade is indeed hard to come by, but as a treasure—even if it were not the Qin seal, and even if it were the genuine Qin seal—what would make it worth prizing?

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，高斌督河時奏進屬員濬寶應河所得玉璽，古澤可愛，又與輟耕錄載蔡仲平本頗合。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, when Gao Bin was supervising the rivers, he memorialized presenting a jade seal obtained by a subordinate while dredging the Bao-ying River; its ancient luster was charming, and it also matched rather closely the Cai Zhongping version recorded in the Record of Cessation of Ploughing.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3, while Gao Bin was supervising river works, he presented a jade seal dredged from the Bao-ying River by a subordinate; its ancient luster was appealing and it closely matched the Cai Zhongping version recorded in the Record of Cessation of Ploughing.

sentences.zh: 朕謂此好事者仿刻所為，貯之別殿，視為玩好舊器而已。

translations.literal: I said that this was the work of some enthusiast's imitation carving; store it in a separate hall and regard it merely as an old curio for enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: I judged it the work of some enthusiast's imitation and ordered it kept in a separate hall as a mere antique curio.

sentences.zh: 夫秦璽煨燼，古人論之詳矣。

translations.literal: As for the Qin seal having been burned to ashes, the ancients discussed this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients discussed at length how the Qin seal was burned to ashes.

sentences.zh: 即使尚存，政、斯之物，何得與本朝傳寶同貯？

translations.literal: Even if it still survived, how could an object of Zhao Zheng and Li Si be stored together with our dynasty's transmitted seals?
translations.idiomatic: Even if it had survived, how could an object belonging to the First Emperor and Li Si be stored with our dynasty's transmitted seals?

sentences.zh: 於義未當。

translations.literal: This would be improper in principle.
translations.idiomatic: That would be improper in principle.

sentences.zh: 又雍正年故大學士高其位進未刻碧玉寶，一文未刻，未成為寶，而與諸寶同貯，亦未當。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Yongzheng reign the late grand secretary Gao Qiwei presented an uncarved green jade seal—not a single character engraved, not yet a seal at all—yet it was stored with the other seals; this too was improper.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, in the Yongzheng reign the late Grand Secretary Gao Qiwei presented an uncarved green jade block—not a single character cut, not yet a seal at all—yet it was stored with the other seals, which was also improper.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗論之，君人者在德不在寶。

translations.literal: I have often discussed this: what matters for a ruler is virtue, not seals.
translations.idiomatic: I have often said that what matters for a ruler is virtue, not seals.

sentences.zh: 寶雖重，一器耳。

translations.literal: Though seals are weighty, they are only objects.
translations.idiomatic: Seals may be weighty symbols, but they are only objects.

sentences.zh: 明等威、徵信守，與車旗章服何異？

translations.literal: They display rank and dignity and attest to trust and good faith—how do they differ from chariots, banners, regalia, and robes?
translations.idiomatic: They display rank and attest to authority, no different from chariots, banners, regalia, and robes.

sentences.zh: 德之不足，則山河之險，土宇之富，拱手而授之他人，未有徒恃此區區尺璧，足以自固者。

translations.literal: When virtue is insufficient, even mountains and rivers as barriers and a rich domain are handed over to others with folded arms; never has anyone relied on this mere foot-square jade disk alone to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Without sufficient virtue, even natural barriers and a rich realm are surrendered to others; no one has ever secured a dynasty by relying on a mere foot-square jade seal alone.

sentences.zh: 誠能勤修令德，系屬人心，則言傳號渙，萬里奔走，珍非和璧，制不龍螭，篆不斯籀，孰敢不敬信承奉，尊為神明。

translations.literal: If one can diligently cultivate excellent virtue and bind the hearts of the people, then a word is transmitted and a title is proclaimed, and men race ten thousand li to obey; whether the treasure is not the He-shi disk, the form is not dragon and chi, or the script is not that of Li Si or Zhou—who would dare not revere, trust, receive, and honor it as divine?
translations.idiomatic: If one diligently cultivates virtue and wins the people's hearts, a word proclaimed will bring men racing from ten thousand li to obey; whether the object is the He-shi jade or not, whether its form bears dragons or not, whether its script is ancient seal or not—who would dare not revere and obey it as sacred?

sentences.zh: 故寶器非寶，寶於有德。

translations.literal: Thus the vessel is not the treasure; virtue is the treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the seal itself is not the treasure; virtue is the true treasure.

sentences.zh: 古有得前代符寶，君臣動色矜耀，侈為瑞貺者。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when former dynasties' tally-seals were obtained, ruler and ministers would change expression and boast, extravagantly treating them as auspicious gifts from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a former dynasty's tally-seals were obtained, ruler and ministers would change countenance and boast, extravagantly calling them Heaven's auspicious gift.

sentences.zh: 我太宗文皇帝時，獲蒙古所傳元帝國寶，容而納之，初不藉以為受命之符。

translations.literal: In the time of our Literary Emperor Taizong, the Yuan emperor's national seal transmitted by the Mongols was obtained and accepted, but from the first it was not relied upon as a token of receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of our Literary Emperor Taizong, the Yuan imperial seal transmitted by the Mongols was obtained and accepted, but from the outset it was not treated as proof of receiving Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 由今思之，文皇帝之臣服函夏，垂統萬世，在德耶？

translations.literal: Reflecting on this today, was the Literary Emperor's bringing all within the Four Seas to submission and bequeathing his line for ten thousand generations due to virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Looking back today, was the Literary Emperor's bringing all China to submission and establishing a line for ten thousand generations due to virtue?

sentences.zh: 在寶耶？

translations.literal: Or due to seals?
translations.idiomatic: Or due to seals?

sentences.zh: 不待智者而知之矣。

translations.literal: One need not wait for a wise man to know the answer.
translations.idiomatic: No wise man is needed to know the answer.

sentences.zh: 善夫唐梁肅之言曰：『鼎之輕重，璽之去來，視德之高下，位之安危。』

translations.literal: Excellent are the words of Liang Su of Tang: "Whether the cauldron is heavy or light, whether the seal comes or goes—all depend on the height or lowness of virtue and the safety or peril of the throne."
translations.idiomatic: How apt are the words of Liang Su of Tang: "Whether the cauldron is heavy or light and whether the seal comes or goes depend on the ruler's virtue and the throne's security."

sentences.zh: 然則人君承祖宗付畀，思以永膺斯寶，引而勿替，其非什襲固守之謂。

translations.literal: Thus when a ruler receives what his ancestors entrusted and thinks to hold this seal forever, extending it without end—this does not mean merely wrapping it in many layers and guarding it fixedly.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler receives what his ancestors entrusted and seeks to hold this seal forever, extending the line without end, that does not mean merely wrapping it in many layers and guarding it in a box.

sentences.zh: 謂夫日新厥德，居安慮危，凝受皇天大寶命，則德足重寶，而寶以愈重。

translations.literal: It means renewing one's virtue daily, being mindful of peril in times of peace, and steadfastly receiving the great mandate of Heaven—then virtue is weighty enough to dignify the seal, and the seal becomes all the weightier.
translations.idiomatic: It means renewing one's virtue daily, being mindful of peril in peace, and steadfastly receiving Heaven's great mandate—then virtue dignifies the seal, and the seal grows all the weightier.

sentences.zh: 璽玉自古無定數，今交泰殿所貯，歷年既久，紀載失真，且有重複者。

translations.literal: Seals and jades have had no fixed number since antiquity; those now stored in the Hall of Union and Peace, after many years, have records that have lost accuracy, and there are duplicates as well.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial seals have never had a fixed number; those kept in the Hall of Union and Peace, after many years, are inaccurately recorded and include duplicates.

sentences.zh: 爰加考正排次，定為二十有五，以符天數。

translations.literal: Therefore I have examined, corrected, and arranged them, fixing the number at twenty-five to accord with the number of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore examined, corrected, and arranged them, fixing the number at twenty-five to accord with Heaven's number.

sentences.zh: 並著成譜，而序其大恉如此。」

translations.literal: I have also compiled a register and set forth its main purport thus."
translations.idiomatic: I also compiled a register and set forth its main purpose as above."

sentences.zh: 又盛京尊藏寶譜序曰：「乾隆十一年春，閱交泰殿所貯諸寶，既詳定位置，為文記之。

translations.literal: The preface to the Register of Seals Reverently Stored in Mukden also says: "In the spring of the eleventh year of Qianlong, having reviewed the seals stored in the Hall of Union and Peace and fixed their positions in detail, I wrote an account of them.
translations.idiomatic: The preface to the Register of Seals Reverently Stored in Mukden also states: "In the spring of Qianlong 11, after reviewing the seals in the Hall of Union and Peace and fixing their positions in detail, I wrote an account of them.

sentences.zh: 其應別貯者，分別收貯。

translations.literal: Those that should be stored separately were put away in separate storage.
translations.idiomatic: Those that should be stored separately were placed in separate storage.

sentences.zh: 至其文或複見，及國初行用者，為數凡十。

translations.literal: As for those whose inscriptions are duplicated or were used at the founding of the state, they number ten in all.
translations.idiomatic: Those with duplicate inscriptions or used at the dynasty's founding number ten in all.

sentences.zh: 雖不同現用之寶，而未可與古玩並列。

translations.literal: Though they differ from the seals in current use, they cannot be classed with antique curios.
translations.idiomatic: Though not the seals in current use, they cannot be classed with mere antique curios.

sentences.zh: 因念盛京為國家發祥地，祖宗神爽，實所式憑。

translations.literal: Reflecting that Mukden is the land where the state arose and that the spirits of the ancestors are truly to be revered there,
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that Mukden is where the state arose and that the ancestral spirits are truly to be revered there,

sentences.zh: 朕既重繕列祖實錄，尊藏鳳凰樓上，覲揚光烈，傳示無疆。

translations.literal: I have already had the Veritable Records of successive ancestors recopied and reverently stored in the Phoenix Tower, displaying their glorious deeds to be transmitted without end.
translations.idiomatic: I have had the Veritable Records of successive ancestors recopied and reverently stored in the Phoenix Tower, displaying their glorious deeds for endless transmission.

sentences.zh: 想當開天之始，凝受帝命，寶符煥發，六服承式，璠興孚尹，手澤存焉。

translations.literal: I think that at the beginning when Heaven was opened, they steadfastly received the imperial mandate; the precious tally blazed forth, the six regions took their model, jade gleamed with inner light, and their hand's touch still remains.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty, they steadfastly received Heaven's mandate; the precious tally blazed forth, the six regions took their model, jade gleamed with inner light, and their touch still lingers on these objects.

sentences.zh: 記不云乎，『陳其宗器』，弘璧琬琰，陳之西序，崇世守也。

translations.literal: Does not the Record say, "Display the ancestral vessels"—great disks and fine jades displayed in the western wing, honoring what is guarded through the generations?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Record say, "Display the ancestral vessels"—great disks and fine jades set out in the western wing, honoring what is guarded through the generations?

sentences.zh: 爰奉此十寶，齎送盛京，鐍而藏之，而著其緣起如此。」

translations.literal: Therefore these ten seals were reverently sent to Mukden, locked away and stored, and their origin is recorded thus."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore these ten seals were sent to Mukden, locked away for safekeeping, and their origin is recorded as above."

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年九月，改鐫御寶，始用清篆文，左為清篆，右為漢篆。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Qianlong, the imperial seals were recut; Manchu seal script was first used, with Manchu seal script on the left and Han seal script on the right.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Qianlong 13, the imperial seals were recut to use Manchu seal script on the left and Han seal script on the right.

sentences.zh: 高宗御題交泰殿寶譜序後曰：「寶譜成於乾隆十一年丙寅，越三年戊辰，始指授儒臣為清文各篆體書。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor's imperial inscription after the preface to the Hall of Union and Peace Seal Register says: "The register was completed in the bingyin year of Qianlong 11; three years later in the wuchen year, I first directed scholar-officials to write the Manchu text in the various seal-script forms.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor inscribed after the register's preface: "The register was completed in Qianlong 11; three years later I first directed scholar-officials to write the Manchu text in the various seal-script forms.

sentences.zh: 因思向之國寶，官印，漢文用篆書，而清文則用本字者，以國書篆體未備也。

translations.literal: Reflecting that formerly on national seals and official seals the Han text used seal script while the Manchu text used the standard characters—this was because Manchu seal script had not yet been prepared.
translations.idiomatic: I reflected that formerly on state and official seals the Han text used seal script while the Manchu text used standard characters, because Manchu seal script had not yet been standardized.

sentences.zh: 今既定為篆法，當施之寶印，以昭畫一。

translations.literal: Now that seal script has been fixed as the standard, it should be applied to seals and stamps to display uniformity.
translations.idiomatic: Now that seal script has been standardized, it should be applied to all seals to display uniformity.

sentences.zh: 按譜內青玉『皇帝之寶』，本清字篆文，傳自太宗文皇帝時，自是而上四寶，均先代相承，傳為世守者，不敢輕易。

translations.literal: According to the register, the bluish jade "Emperor's Seal" originally bore Manchu seal script and was transmitted from the time of the Literary Emperor Taizong; the four seals above it were all handed down from former generations as heirlooms and could not be lightly altered.
translations.idiomatic: The bluish jade "Emperor's Seal" in the register originally bore Manchu seal script and dates from the Literary Emperor Taizong; the four seals above it were all dynastic heirlooms and could not be lightly altered.

sentences.zh: 其檀香『皇帝之寶』以下二十有一，則朝儀綸綍所常用，宜從新制。

translations.literal: The twenty-one from the sandalwood "Emperor's Seal" downward are those commonly used in court ritual and edicts and should follow the new standard.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-one seals from the sandalwood "Emperor's Seal" downward are those commonly used in court ritual and edicts and should follow the new standard.

sentences.zh: 因敕所司一律改鐫，與漢篆文相配，並記之寶譜序後雲。」

translations.literal: Therefore I ordered the responsible offices to recut them all uniformly, paired with the Han seal script, and recorded this after the register's preface."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ordered the responsible offices to recut them all uniformly, paired with the Han seal script, and recorded this after the register's preface."

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年八月，高宗七旬聖壽，用杜甫句刻「古稀天子之寶」，並御制古稀說，兼系以詩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the forty-fifth year of Qianlong, on the Gaozong Emperor's seventieth birthday, a line from Du Fu was carved as "Seal of the Son of Heaven at Seventy," together with an imperial composition "On Being Seventy" and an appended poem.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Qianlong 45, on the Qianlong Emperor's seventieth birthday, a line from Du Fu was carved as the "Seal of the Son of Heaven at Seventy," together with an imperial essay "On Being Seventy" and an appended poem.

sentences.zh: 四十六年正月，用乾清宮西暖閣貯「敬天勤民寶」之例，貯「古稀天子之寶」於東暖閣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-sixth year, following the precedent of storing the "Seal of Revering Heaven and Diligently Serving the People" in the west warm chamber of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, the "Seal of the Son of Heaven at Seventy" was stored in the east warm chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 46, following the precedent of keeping the "Seal of Revering Heaven and Diligently Serving the People" in the west warm chamber of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, the "Seal of the Son of Heaven at Seventy" was kept in the east warm chamber.

sentences.zh: 皇后金寶，清、漢文玉箸篆，交龍紐，平台，方四寸四分，厚一寸二分。

translations.literal: The empress's golden seal: Manchu and Han jade-stylus seal script, intertwined-dragon knob, flat platform, four cun four fen square, one cun two fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's golden seal bears Manchu and Han jade-stylus seal script, with an intertwined-dragon knob on a flat platform, four cun four fen square and one cun two fen thick.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，制太皇太后金寶、玉寶，盤龍紐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, golden and jade seals for the grand empress dowager were made, with coiled-dragon knobs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4, golden and jade seals for the grand empress dowager were made with coiled-dragon knobs.

sentences.zh: 餘皆與皇后寶同。

translations.literal: The rest are the same as the empress's seals.
translations.idiomatic: The rest match the empress's seals in form.

sentences.zh: 玉寶台高一寸八分，餘同金寶。

translations.literal: The jade seal's platform is one cun eight fen high; the rest is the same as the golden seal.
translations.idiomatic: The jade seal's platform is one cun eight fen high; otherwise it matches the golden seal.

sentences.zh: 皇太后金寶、玉寶，俱盤龍紐。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's golden and jade seals both have coiled-dragon knobs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's golden and jade seals both have coiled-dragon knobs.

sentences.zh: 餘與皇后寶同。

translations.literal: The rest is the same as the empress's seals.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they match the empress's seals.

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃金寶，清、漢文玉箸篆，蹲龍紐，平台，方四寸，厚一寸二分。

translations.literal: The imperial noble consort's golden seal: Manchu and Han jade-stylus seal script, crouching-dragon knob, flat platform, four cun square, one cun two fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial noble consort's golden seal bears Manchu and Han jade-stylus seal script, with a crouching-dragon knob on a flat platform, four cun square and one cun two fen thick.

sentences.zh: 貴妃金寶，與皇貴妃同。

translations.literal: The noble consort's golden seal is the same as the imperial noble consort's.
translations.idiomatic: The noble consort's golden seal matches the imperial noble consort's.

sentences.zh: 妃金印，清、漢文玉箸篆，龜紐，平台，方三寸六分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: The consort's golden stamp: Manchu and Han jade-stylus seal script, tortoise knob, flat platform, three cun six fen square, one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: The consort's golden stamp bears Manchu and Han jade-stylus seal script, with a tortoise knob on a flat platform, three cun six fen square and one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，定皇太子金寶，玉箸篆，蹲龍紐，平台，方四寸，厚一寸二分。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi, the crown prince's golden seal was fixed: jade-stylus seal script, crouching-dragon knob, flat platform, four cun square, one cun two fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15, the crown prince's golden seal was standardized: jade-stylus seal script, crouching-dragon knob, flat platform, four cun square and one cun two fen thick.

sentences.zh: 和碩親王金寶，龜紐，平台，方三寸六分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: The prince of the first rank's golden seal: tortoise knob, flat platform, three cun six fen square, one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of the first rank's golden seal has a tortoise knob on a flat platform, three cun six fen square and one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 親王世子金寶，龜紐，平台，方三寸五分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: The prince's heir's golden seal: tortoise knob, flat platform, three cun five fen square, one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: A prince's heir's golden seal has a tortoise knob on a flat platform, three cun five fen square and one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 多羅郡王鍍金銀印，麒麟紐，平台，方三寸四分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: The prince of the second rank's gilt-silver stamp: qilin knob, flat platform, three cun four fen square, one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: A prince of the second rank's gilt-silver stamp has a qilin knob on a flat platform, three cun four fen square and one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 俱清、漢文芝英篆。

translations.literal: All bear Manchu and Han mushroom-tip seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All bear Manchu and Han mushroom-tip seal script.

sentences.zh: 外國王鍍金銀印，清、漢文尚方大篆，駝紐，平台，方三寸五分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: Foreign kings' gilt-silver stamps: Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script, camel knob, flat platform, three cun five fen square, one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign kings' gilt-silver stamps bear Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script, with a camel knob on a flat platform, three cun five fen square and one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 順治十年，以朝鮮國王原領印文有清字無漢字，命禮部改鑄清、漢文金印，頒給該王，仍將舊印繳進。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi, because the King of Korea's original seal inscription had Manchu characters but no Han characters, the Ministry of Rites was ordered to recast a golden seal in Manchu and Han and present it to that king, while the old seal was still to be surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10, because the King of Korea's original seal had Manchu but no Han characters, the Ministry of Rites was ordered to recast a Manchu-and-Han golden seal for him and require surrender of the old one.

sentences.zh: 知宗人府、衍聖公銀印，直紐，三台，方三寸三分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: The seals of the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Duke of Yansheng: straight knob, three-tier base, three cun three fen square, one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Clan and the Duke of Yansheng used silver seals with straight knobs and three-tier bases, three cun three fen square and one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 俱清、漢文尚方大篆。

translations.literal: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script.

sentences.zh: 公、侯、伯銀印，虎紐，方三寸三分，厚九分。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, and earls' silver stamps: tiger knob, three cun three fen square, nine fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, and earls used silver stamps with tiger knobs, three cun three fen square and nine fen thick.

sentences.zh: 公三台，侯、伯二台。

translations.literal: Dukes have three-tier bases; marquises and earls have two-tier bases.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes had three-tier bases; marquises and earls had two-tier bases.

sentences.zh: 經略大臣、大將軍、將軍、領侍衛內大臣銀印，虎紐，二台，方三寸三分，厚九分。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators, grand generals, generals, and leading grand ministers of the guard's silver stamps: tiger knob, two-tier base, three cun three fen square, nine fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators, grand generals, generals, and leading grand ministers of the guard used silver stamps with tiger knobs and two-tier bases, three cun three fen square and nine fen thick.

sentences.zh: 俱清、漢文柳葉篆。

translations.literal: All bear Manchu and Han willow-leaf seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All bear Manchu and Han willow-leaf seal script.

sentences.zh: 軍機事務處銀印，直紐，二台，方三寸二分，厚八分。

translations.literal: The Grand Council's silver stamp: straight knob, two-tier base, three cun two fen square, eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council's silver stamp had a straight knob and two-tier base, three cun two fen square and eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年四月，改軍機處為內閣，舊內閣遂裁。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Xuantong, the Grand Council was changed to the Grand Secretariat, and the old Grand Secretariat was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xuantong 3, the Grand Council was renamed the Grand Secretariat, and the old Grand Secretariat was abolished.

sentences.zh: 主各部、都察院銀印，直紐，三台，方三寸三分，厚九分。

translations.literal: The supervising seals of the ministries and the Censorate: straight knob, three-tier base, three cun three fen square, nine fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising seals of the ministries and the Censorate had straight knobs and three-tier bases, three cun three fen square and nine fen thick.

sentences.zh: 俱清、漢文尚方大篆。

translations.literal: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script.

sentences.zh: 理籓院銀印，直紐，三台，方三寸三分，厚九分。

translations.literal: The Court of Colonial Affairs' silver stamp: straight knob, three-tier base, three cun three fen square, nine fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Colonial Affairs' silver stamp had a straight knob and three-tier base, three cun three fen square and nine fen thick.

sentences.zh: 兼清、漢、蒙古三體字，清、漢文尚方大篆，蒙古字不用篆。

translations.literal: It includes Manchu, Han, and Mongolian in three scripts; Manchu and Han use Shangfang large seal script, while Mongolian does not use seal script.
translations.idiomatic: It bore Manchu, Han, and Mongolian in three scripts; Manchu and Han used Shangfang large seal script, while Mongolian did not.

sentences.zh: 理籓院後改理籓部。

translations.literal: The Court of Colonial Affairs was later changed to the Ministry of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Colonial Affairs was later renamed the Ministry of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 主盛京五部銀印，直紐，二台，方三寸二分，厚八分。

translations.literal: The supervising seals of the Five Boards in Mukden: straight knob, two-tier base, three cun two fen square, eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising seals of the Five Boards in Mukden had straight knobs and two-tier bases, three cun two fen square and eight fen thick.

translations.literal: The Five Boards in Mukden were later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Boards in Mukden were later abolished.

translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue's seal for supervising the three treasuries had a straight knob and two-tier base, three cun two fen square and eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 戶部後改名度支部。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue was later renamed the Ministry of Finance.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was later renamed the Ministry of Finance.

sentences.zh: 齋翰林院銀印，二台，方三寸二分，厚八分。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academy's silver stamp: two-tier base, three cun two fen square, eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academy's silver stamp had a two-tier base, three cun two fen square and eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 內務府銀印，二台，方三寸二分，厚八分。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household Department's silver stamp: two-tier base, three cun two fen square, eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household Department's silver stamp had a two-tier base, three cun two fen square and eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 景陵、泰陵內務府總管，東陵、泰陵承辦事務銅關防，凡關防皆直紐。

translations.literal: The copper chops of the Imperial Household superintendents at the Jing and Tai mausoleums, and the transaction superintendents at the Eastern and Tai mausoleums—all chops have straight knobs.
translations.idiomatic: The copper chops of the Imperial Household superintendents at the Jing and Tai mausoleums and the transaction superintendents at the Eastern and Tai mausoleums—all chops have straight knobs.

sentences.zh: 長三寸，闊一寸九分。

translations.literal: Length three cun, width one cun nine fen.
translations.idiomatic: They measure three cun long and one cun nine fen wide.

sentences.zh: 鑾儀衛銀印，直紐，二台，方三寸二分，厚八分。

translations.literal: The Imperial Procession Guard's silver stamp: straight knob, two-tier base, three cun two fen square, eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Procession Guard's silver stamp had a straight knob and two-tier base, three cun two fen square and eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 宣統朝因避寫故名鑾輿衛。

translations.literal: In the Xuantong reign, to avoid taboo writing it was renamed the Imperial Carriage Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuantong reign, it was renamed the Imperial Carriage Guard to avoid a taboo character.

translations.literal: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang large seal script.

translations.literal: The supervising silver stamps of the Office of Transmission, Court of Judicature and Revision, Court of State Ceremonial, Shuntian Prefecture, and Shengjing Prefecture: straight knob, two cun nine fen square, six fen five li thick.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising silver stamps of the Office of Transmission, Court of Judicature and Revision, Court of State Ceremonial, Shuntian Prefecture, and Shengjing Prefecture had straight knobs, two cun nine fen square and six fen five li thick.

translations.idiomatic: The Office of Transmission was later abolished, the Court of Judicature and Revision was renamed the Court of Judicature, and the Court of State Ceremonial was merged into the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 俱清、漢文尚方小篆。

translations.literal: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang small seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All bear Manchu and Han Shangfang small seal script.

sentences.zh: 齋詹事府銅印，直紐，方二寸七分，厚九分。

translations.literal: Also included: the Household of the Heir Apparent's copper stamp, straight knob, two cun seven fen square, nine fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Household of the Heir Apparent also had a copper stamp with a straight knob, two cun seven fen square and nine fen thick.

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Stud, Armory, Upper Stud Office, and Fengchen Garden copper stamps: straight knob, two cun six fen square, six fen five li thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments, Court of the Imperial Stud, Armory, Upper Stud Office, and Fengchen Garden used copper stamps with straight knobs, two cun six fen square and six fen five li thick.

sentences.zh: 詹事府後裁，光祿寺後歸併禮部，太僕寺後歸併陸軍部。

translations.idiomatic: The Household of the Heir Apparent was later abolished, the Court of Imperial Entertainments was merged into the Ministry of Rites, and the Court of the Imperial Stud was merged into the Ministry of the Army.

sentences.zh: 古內繙書房銅關防，長三寸，闊一寸九分，俱清、漢文尚方小篆。

translations.literal: The former Inner Translation Office's copper chop: length three cun, width one cun nine fen; all bear Manchu and Han Shangfang small seal script.
translations.idiomatic: The former Inner Translation Office's copper chop measured three cun long and one cun nine fen wide, bearing Manchu and Han Shangfang small seal script.

translations.literal: The Directorate of Education's copper stamp: straight knob, two cun five fen square, six fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Education's copper stamp had a straight knob, two cun five fen square and six fen thick.

translations.literal: The Imperial Medical Academy's copper stamp: straight knob, two cun four fen square, five fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Medical Academy's copper stamp had a straight knob, two cun four fen square and five fen thick.

sentences.zh: 各道監察御史、稽察內務府御史、稽察宗人府御史、巡鹽御史銅印，直紐，有孔，方一寸五分，厚三分。

translations.literal: The circuit censors, censors inspecting the Imperial Household Department, censors inspecting the Court of the Imperial Clan, and salt-patrol censors' copper stamps: straight knob, with hole, one cun five fen square, three fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit censors, censors inspecting the Imperial Household Department and Court of the Imperial Clan, and salt-patrol censors used copper stamps with straight knobs and perforations, one cun five fen square and three fen thick.

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Clan's left and right offices, Court of the Imperial Stud's left and right offices, Imperial Procession Guard's left and right offices, and the various offices of the ministries and Court of Colonial Affairs' copper stamps: straight knob, two cun four fen square, five fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right offices of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Court of the Imperial Stud, and Imperial Procession Guard, together with the various offices of the ministries and Court of Colonial Affairs, used copper stamps with straight knobs, two cun four fen square and five fen thick.

sentences.zh: 內務府各司銅印，直紐，方二寸二分，厚四分五釐。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household Department's various offices' copper stamps: straight knob, two cun two fen square, four fen five li thick.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices of the Imperial Household Department used copper stamps with straight knobs, two cun two fen square and four fen five li thick.

translations.idiomatic: These included the Chongwen Gate tax administration, the Revenue Ministry's Grain-Ration Hall sub-office, and Works Ministry supervisors of timber fuel, timber yards, and street warehouses; the Works Ministry was later renamed and merged into the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce.

translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Bureau's calendar-book copper stamp had a straight knob, two cun one fen square and four fen four li thick.

translations.idiomatic: The official-house tax treasuries of the Changchun Garden, Old Summer Palace, and Clear Ripples Garden used copper strip marks; all strip marks have straight knobs.

sentences.zh: 長二寸六分，闊一寸九分。

translations.literal: Length two cun six fen, width one cun nine fen.
translations.idiomatic: They measure two cun six fen long and one cun nine fen wide.

sentences.zh: 俱清、漢文鐘鼎篆。

translations.literal: All bear Manchu and Han bell-and-cauldron seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All bear Manchu and Han bell-and-cauldron seal script.

translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Office's copper stamp had a straight knob, two cun one fen square and four fen five li thick.

translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat Records Office's copper chop measured three cun long and one cun nine fen wide.

sentences.zh: 翰林院典簿，禮部鑄印局，宣統三年印鑄局改屬新內閣，禮部亦改典禮院。

sentences.zh: 觀於印譜，而群才翊運之殷又可知。

translations.literal: From viewing the seal register, the abundance of talented men assisting the dynasty is likewise knowable.
translations.idiomatic: From viewing the seal register, the abundance of talented men assisting the dynasty is likewise knowable.

sentences.zh: 詩曰：『王之藎臣，無念爾祖。』

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'O king's devoted ministers, do not forget your ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: 'O king's devoted ministers, do not forget your ancestors.

sentences.zh: 記曰：『君子聽鼓鼙，則思將帥之臣。』

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: "When the gentleman hears drums and military banners, he thinks of generals and commanders."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: "When the gentleman hears drums and military banners, he thinks of generals and commanders."

sentences.zh: 一再披閱，其何能置大風猛士之懷哉！

translations.literal: Reading it again and again — how can one put aside thoughts of mighty wind and fierce soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: To read it again and again — how could one set aside thoughts of mighty warriors and fierce soldiers!

sentences.zh: 裝潢蕆事，並令守者什襲尊藏。

translations.literal: When binding and mounting are complete, those charged with keeping them shall store them with tenfold care.
